summary.en: Explore a state-space tree, undo each choice, and prune prefixes that cannot reach a valid answer.
summary.bn: একটা পছন্দ করে এগোও, ফিরে এসে সেটা সরাও, আর যেসব পথে উত্তর মিলবে না সেগুলো বাদ দাও।

notes: The demonstrated programs use C17; the lesson states their input and arithmetic bounds.

sections.title: Reject a prefix for a reason
Depth is smaller than the whole tree
First answer, all answers, and no answers
An early return can leave damage

examples.title: Enumerate a fixed number of ones
examples.explanationHtml: With input 4 2, the recursive search prints 0011, 0101, 0110, 1001, 1010 and 1100. Each row is a different complete path. Input 0 0 prints one empty line: the empty string is a valid candidate.

examples.title: Count the unpruned tree
examples.explanationHtml: For depth four, the loop reports sixteen leaves and thirty-one total nodes. Adding the sizes of all levels explains why visiting internal prefixes matters too.

examples.title: Pass a prefix by value
examples.explanationHtml: The numeric-prefix example prints zero through seven for depth three. Multiplying by two appends a binary zero; adding one chooses a binary one. A value parameter avoids shared-counter restoration.

practice.title: Draw all binary prefixes of length two and identify the leaves.
practice.statementHtml: Draw all binary prefixes of length two and identify the leaves.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: The root is empty. Its children are 0 and 1. Their children are 00, 01, 10 and 11. Four leaves correspond to four complete decisions.

practice.title: For length five with exactly two ones, justify both pruning conditions.
practice.statementHtml: For length five with exactly two ones, justify both pruning conditions.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: Reject used > 2 because adding bits cannot remove a one. Reject used + 5 - pos < 2 because even choosing one at every remaining position falls short. Both arguments rule out every completion.

quiz.prompt: What does one edge in the binary state-space tree represent?
quiz.explanation: The edge fixes the next position; only a leaf fixes every position.

quiz.prompt: Why restore path[pos] after exploring a binary choice?
options: To count the same leaf twice
quiz.explanation: Undo removes branch-specific state before a sibling uses that slot.

quiz.prompt: At pos=3, n=5, used=0 and ones=3, why can the branch stop?
quiz.explanation: At most two more ones can be added, short of the required three.

quiz.prompt: Which prune is valid when exactly two ones are required?
options: Reject a prefix with one one
quiz.explanation: Further choices cannot reduce used, so an excess is permanent.

quiz.prompt: How many leaves are in an unpruned binary tree of depth four?
quiz.explanation: Each of four independent decisions doubles the leaves; 31 counts all nodes.

quiz.prompt: What changes when you only need the first valid candidate?
options: Return a success flag up the calls
quiz.explanation: A success flag can stop siblings once one valid full path is found.

quiz.prompt: Which claim about pruning is justified?
options: It can reduce work without changing answers
quiz.explanation: A sound prune removes only branches with no required answers; worst-case growth may remain exponential.

quiz.prompt: In a depth-three decision tree, how many complete binary choices does this loop count?
quiz.explanation: Three doublings give eight leaves; fifteen would include internal nodes.

quiz.prompt: What value remains after this choice is explicitly undone?
quiz.explanation: The increment belongs to the child; the decrement restores its parent state.

quiz.prompt: How many length-four branches contain exactly two one bits?
quiz.explanation: Choose two of the four positions: 4*3/2 gives six leaves.

keyPoints.en: A state records the decisions made along one path.
keyPoints.bn: একটা স্টেট এক পথের আগের সিদ্ধান্তগুলো ধরে রাখে।

keyPoints.en: Choose, explore, and undo keep sibling branches independent.
keyPoints.bn: পছন্দ করে এগোও, তারপর পছন্দটা সরাও; তাতে পাশের পথ আলাদা থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Pruning needs a reason that covers every possible completion.
keyPoints.bn: কোনো পথ বাদ দিতে হলে দেখাতে হবে, সেই পথে আর উত্তর মিলবে না।

keyPoints.en: A base case decides whether a complete candidate should be reported.
keyPoints.bn: base case-এ ঠিক করো, পুরো উত্তরটা দেখাবে কি না।

keyPoints.en: Exponential search can be useful when the decision count is small.
keyPoints.bn: সিদ্ধান্ত কম থাকলে exponential সার্চও কাজে লাগে।

examQuestions.question: Draw all binary prefixes of length two and identify the leaves.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The root is empty. Its children are 0 and 1. Their children are 00, 01, 10 and 11. Four leaves correspond to four complete decisions.

examQuestions.question: For length five with exactly two ones, justify both pruning conditions.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Reject used > 2 because adding bits cannot remove a one. Reject used + 5 - pos < 2 because even choosing one at every remaining position falls short. Both arguments rule out every completion.

examQuestions.question: State the invariant and justify the time and space costs of Introduction to Backtracking.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
The invariant is that the chosen prefix contains exactly used ones when a call starts. Choosing bit b extends the prefix by one and changes that count to used+b. Thus the child receives a truthful state. Returning and undoing restores the parent's prefix before a sibling starts.

For completeness, take any valid full string. Its prefixes never exceed the required ones, and each has enough remaining positions to finish. Neither pruning test rejects them. The search tries both bits at every surviving position, so it eventually follows that whole string.

For uniqueness, two different paths first differ at some bit. They cannot produce the same full binary string. A complete surviving prefix has exactly the required count, so every reported string is valid. These arguments establish validity, completeness and no duplicate reports separately.

Without pruning, depth n gives 2^n leaves and 2^(n+1)-1 nodes. Visiting nodes alone takes O(2^n) time. Printing each length-n answer adds O(n) per answer, so O(n*2^n) is a safe overall bound.

The active recursion stack has only one root-to-leaf path, not every node. It needs O(n) space together with the path array. If you store every answer instead of printing immediately, retained output can require O(n*2^n) memory.

Pruning often makes individual instances much smaller. It does not turn every combinatorial search into a polynomial algorithm. Counting required-one strings can also use a binomial formula, but that formula does not list their actual contents.
